مَائِرَاتٌ Bloods [flowing, and running hither and thither]. So in the following verse (of Rusheyd Ibn-Rumeyd El-'Anazee, TA; not of El-Aashà [as it is said to be in the S in art. عوض;] Sgh, in TA, art. عوض:) “حَلَفْتُ بِمَائِرَاتٍ حَوْلَ عَوْضٍ
وَأَنْصَابٍ تُرِكْنَ لَدَى السَّعِيرِ
” [or السُّعَيْرِ, i. e., I swore, or I swear, by bloods flowing and running hither and thither, around 'Owd, and stones set up to be worshipped, left by Es-Sa'eer or Es-So'eyr]. 'Owd and Es-Sa'eer [or Es-So'eyr] were two idols. (S, TA.) [See also another verse, cited in art. عز.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
